tokens._note: The frame is a light, terracotta-brand consumer mobile surface. arc's tokens.css is a dark, indigo-brand developer cockpit. None of the frame's literal values exist in tokens.css today — the mapping below pairs each Figma value with the tokens.css SEMANTIC SLOT it belongs in, so this screen should ship as a new theme scope (e.g. [data-theme="food-order-light"]) that re-binds those slots rather than inventing parallel variable names.

colors.role: Primary text: location name, category label (inactive), restaurant name, rating value, status-bar glyphs
colors.notes: tokens.css --fg is #e7ecf5 (arc-dark) / #0e1422 (arc-light). Closest existing slot; re-bind under the new theme scope.

colors.role: Secondary text: card description, tag text, delivery-time text, unsaved heart icon
Tertiary text: 'DELIVERING TO' eyebrow, search placeholder, review count
Terracotta brand: active pill, promo badge, Order Now button, See All, cuisine label, pin/chevron/filter icons, saved heart
colors.notes: tokens.css --brand is #7c8cff. This is the single most important re-bind.
NOT present in the frame — no hover/pressed state was designed. Value proposed by arc (brand darkened ~10%). Needs designer confirmation.

colors.role: Card background, page background, text on brand fills
Subtle fill: search input, inactive category pill, tag pill, delivery badge
Hairline borders: search input, inactive pills, tags, save button, card divider Line
colors.notes: MISSING from the frame's declared tokens.colors list even though it is the most-used stroke in the design. Recovered from raw fill data (rgb 0.953/0.957/0.965).
Semantically this is an amber accent, not a warning. Consider a dedicated --rating slot rather than overloading --warn.

colors.role: 2px inside stroke around the header avatar
colors.notes: MISSING from the frame's declared tokens.colors list. Recovered from raw stroke data (rgb 0.992/0.949/0.933). It is a brand tint — could be expressed as color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 12%, white).

families.role: Display: location name, promo headline, '50%', section heading, restaurant name
families.notes: tokens.css binds --font-display-face to 'Space Grotesk'. Must be overridden for this surface; Outfit is on Google Fonts.
tokens.css binds --font-body to 'Inter'. Figtree is on Google Fonts.

scale.usage: eyebrow (uppercase), tags, delivery time, 'Free Delivery', 'OFF NOW'
search placeholder, category labels, rating value, 'See All', card description (21px leading)

radii.notes: tokens.css has no 6px slot (--radius-control is 7px — close enough to reuse).
tokens.css --radius-control is 7px; needs re-bind to 12px for this surface.

spacing.notes: Consistent 4px-based scale. Page gutter is 20px everywhere except the status bar, which uses 24px.

shadows.notes: Slot exists; value must be re-bound (arc's is a dark-surface shadow).

gradients.name: promo-scrim
gradients.usage: Layered over the promo-banner photo (imageRef 0785bd1b…) to keep white text legible

icons.confidence: high — every Figma icon frame name is an exact lucide export name
icons.notes: Category and nav icons are 2px stroked outlines; star / clock / heart are solid fills.

component_map.notes: Device chrome, not product UI. browser-frame is the catalogue's only viewport-shell primitive; it needs a `mobile` variant (iOS clock left, signal/wifi/battery right, 44px tall, 24px gutters). In production this row is drawn by the OS — render it only in prototypes/screenshots.

props.className: flex items-center justify-between px-5 pt-3 pb-4

component_map.notes: Plain flex row. Figma: HORIZONTAL / SPACE_BETWEEN / CENTER, padding 12 20 16 20.
Figma stores characters as 'Delivering to' with textCase: UPPER — render the mixed-case string and uppercase via CSS so the accessible name stays readable.

Semantically a location picker. Needs a `bare`/ghost trigger variant — the Figma trigger has no background, border, or padding, just icon + 16px Outfit Bold text + chevron with 4px gaps. The option list itself is NOT in this frame.
No avatar primitive in the catalogue. 40×40, circular, object-fit cover, 2px inside ring in #FDF2EE. Frame has no fallback/initials state designed — needed before build.

48px tall, radius 16, --surface-2 fill, --border hairline, 16px side padding, 12px gap. Needs leading/trailing adornment slots if Input doesn't have them. In the frame this is a static row — on a home screen it usually navigates to a search view rather than accepting inline typing; confirm intended behaviour.
18px brand-coloured icon. Rendered with no hit-target padding in Figma (18×18) — enlarge to ≥44×44 for touch without changing visual size.

Thin wrapper: horizontal overflow-x scroller, 8px gap, 20px left padding, 24px bottom padding, clipsContent, no visible scrollbar. Could stay as plain markup — proposed as a component only because the scroll-snap + selection state repeats. `tabs` is the wrong primitive (these are filters, not view switches).
Brand fill, white icon + white 14px SemiBold label, radius 100, padding 10/16, 8px gap. Existing .chip is 10px uppercase mono — this needs a larger `filter` size (14px sentence-case body font).

component_map.figma_node: category-pill · unselected (89:210 Sushi, 89:214 Burgers, 89:218 Healthy, 89:222 Desserts, 89:226 Indian)
component_map.notes: --surface-2 fill, --border hairline, brand-coloured icon, --fg label. Same size variant as above. Six categories total; only 3.5 fit in the 390px viewport, so horizontal scroll is required, not optional.

Card must support a photo fill + gradient scrim + light-on-dark content. Layout is SPACE_BETWEEN: copy block left (200px fixed), '50% / OFF NOW' block right. No `href`/press target is defined in the frame — confirm whether the whole banner is tappable.
Solid brand fill, white 11px ExtraBold, radius 6, padding 4/8.

AMBIGUITY: a 390×145 empty frame at y=70–215 that OVERLAPS promo-banner (y=53–183). It is not a sibling gap — it is a Figma canvas artifact. Do not translate to markup; the real spacing between the banner and the feed is the section's own padding.
Outfit ExtraBold 20/25.2. Should be the section's <h2>.
Brand-coloured Figtree Bold 14, no chrome. Destination not specified in the frame.

component_map.figma_node: restaurant-card (89:243 Bella Cucina, 89:281 Sakura Premium Sushi)
component_map.notes: White surface, radius 24, clipsContent (gallery bleeds to the edge), shadow 0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.031), NO border. Body padding is 20 all round with 16px stack gap.

Three equal-width images (115.33px each) with 2px gutters, object-fit cover, top corners clipped by the parent card. Exactly 3 images in both instances — confirm whether the count is fixed or the component must handle 1/2/4+.
14px / 21px (150%) Figtree Regular. No line-clamp in the frame — card 1 runs 4 lines, card 2 runs 3. Confirm whether long copy should clamp.
Figma layoutWrap: WRAP with 8px on both axes. Both instances happen to wrap to 2 rows.

Static, non-interactive: --surface-2 fill, --border hairline, --muted 12px Medium text, radius 100, padding 6/10. Visually identical to the unselected category pill but smaller and without an icon — same Chip, different size.

ORDERING CONCERN: in the Figma child order this block sits AFTER description and tags-row, so the restaurant name — the card's heading — is announced third. Recommend a visually-identical CSS `order` swap so the DOM leads with the name.
Figtree Medium 13, brand colour, middot-separated: 'Italian · Pizza · Pasta'.

Small composite: 14px filled amber star + 14px Bold value + 13px --faint '(2.4k)' with 6px gaps. Could stay inline markup; proposed as a component because it will recur on the restaurant detail screen. Only a single filled star is drawn — this is a numeric rating, not a 5-star widget.
--surface-2 fill, no border, radius 6, padding 4/8, 6px gap, 12px SemiBold --muted text. Note the en-dash (–) in the range, not a hyphen.
Brand-coloured text with no chrome — deliberately NOT a Badge. Free and paid delivery use the identical treatment, so 'free' carries no extra emphasis; flag to the designer if that's unintended.
Figma LINE node, 1px, --border. Decorative — use role="presentation".
layoutGrow 1 (fills remaining width), 44px tall, radius 12, brand fill, white 15px Bold, shadow 0 4px 12px rgba(226,114,91,.165). No hover/pressed/disabled/loading states are designed.

44×44, radius 12, --border hairline, transparent fill. TWO STATES are drawn: card 1's heart is filled brand #E2725B (saved), card 2's is filled --muted #4B5563 (unsaved). Needs aria-pressed; the unsaved icon should arguably be an outline heart, not a grey solid — worth confirming.

Every icon is wrapped in a centred fixed-size frame. Collapse these wrappers into the icon's own size prop — do not reproduce them as DOM nodes. Adds a lucide-react dependency if the project doesn't already have one.

card → media variant (photo fill + gradient scrim)
